query: For an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy in its uniform, fine lamellar state, whose strength and plasticity remain below industrial application requirements, what single intervention could improve performance for fasteners exposed to extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive conditions? State the proposed intervention, mechanism, predicted outcome relative to the starting alloy, applicable operating and test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit falsification criteria.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a dense, duplex TiN/CrN nanocomposite surface coating to the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy will significantly enhance its performance under extreme thermal cycling, prolonged mechanical loading, room‐temperature creep, and corrosive conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: A uniform, fine-lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy that exhibits strength and plasticity levels below industrial benchmarks.
generation.intervention: Deposit a duplex TiN/CrN nanocomposite coating via physical vapor deposition (PVD).
generation.conditions: Service involves rapid temperature fluctuations (from room temperature up to moderate-high temperatures below ~600°C), long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep stresses, and exposure to corrosive environments.
generation.structural_mediator: A tightly adherent, dense duplex nanocomposite coating that limits surface degradation and provides additional surface hardening.
generation.mechanism: The coating acts as a barrier to oxidation and corrosion while increasing surface yield strength and constraining dislocation motion. This protects the underlying material from environmental attacks and mechanically induced damage (e.g., creep and fatigue) by delaying crack initiation and propagating microstructural damage.
generation.predicted_outcome: The coated alloy is predicted to display higher yield strength, reduced creep rates, improved corrosion resistance, and enhanced overall durability under cyclic thermal and mechanical conditions relative to the uncoated material.
generation.baseline: The performance of the uncoated, uniform, fine-lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy under the same test conditions.
generation.boundary: Improvements will be realized as long as the coating remains intact with good adhesion and is operated within the thermal stability range of the duplex coating (approximately up to 600°C). Beyond these conditions or with premature coating degradation, benefits may diminish.
generation.uncertainty: While the protective and strengthening roles of similar nanocomposite coatings are well-documented in harsh environments, the quantitative gains in plasticity and long-term mechanical behavior for this specific alloy require experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two groups of fastener samples: one group with the duplex TiN/CrN coating applied by PVD and a control group without coating. Subject both sets to standardized testing regimes that include rapid thermal cycling, prolonged mechanical loading (including creep tests at room temperature), and exposure to a corrosive electrolyte under accelerated conditions.
measurements: Tensile and fatigue tests to assess yield strength and ductility.
Long-term creep rate measurement at room temperature under constant load.
Electrochemical corrosion tests (e.g., potentiodynamic polarization) to measure corrosion rates.
Surface analysis for coating adhesion and thickness before and after testing.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coated samples do not show statistically significant improvements (i.e., increases in yield strength and corrosion/creep resistance beyond an industrially relevant threshold) compared to the uncoated controls under the tested conditions, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.
